registered: 2026-11-14, before the recorded profiling run (a development pilot on 100K documents and 3 queries was used only to learn the export formats; it is not a result)
recording: not recorded by the team runtime; self-recorded manifest; runtime gates satisfied by the same local stand-in as the paired experiment
question: Where does the range scorer's time go, and how much of its 4.25x paired advantage over the adapted monolithic baseline is GPU work versus host-side (Python/Torch/launch) overhead?
workload: cuda5 RTX 4070, CUDA 12.6; 1M documents; first 25 calibration queries; k=10; batch 1; range size 4096; 256 score and merge threads; monolithic BLOCK_PL 512
sources: range scorer byte-identical to eef8302; monolithic code byte-identical to the paired experiment's copy (714b8b0); no source changes

nsight_systems.settings: --trace=cuda --sample=none --cpuctxsw=none; one process each; 3 warm-up + 20 measured rounds over the 25 queries; driver argv as in the paired run except --limit 25
nsight_systems.per_query: GPU busy = sum of kernel, memcpy and memset durations; GPU span; host time inside the CUDA calls that launched the query's GPU work; per-kernel and per-copy breakdown; medians over the 20 measured rounds
nsight_systems.query_split: trace cut at the last device-to-host copy of each query (range 1, monolithic 2); group count must equal the driver's row count; warm-up groups (which absorb index upload) are dropped
nsight_systems.primary: geometric mean over the 25 queries of GPU-busy ratio range / monolithic, with a 10,000-draw query bootstrap (seed 20261115)
nsight_systems.secondary: unprofiled wall ratio on the same 25 queries from the paired run; non-GPU time = unprofiled wall median - profiled GPU busy median, per implementation

nsight_compute.program: range scorer, 1 round over the 25 queries (25 launches of each kernel)
nsight_compute.lock: private TMPDIR because /tmp/nsight-compute-lock belongs to another user; therefore no serialisation with other users' Nsight Compute sessions beyond the idle check
nsight_compute.phase_split: warp-state samples per SASS instruction mapped to phases (setup, term lookup, zeroing + first barrier, decode/add incl. prefix sums and shared atomics, local top-k, merge) by CUDA source line, or for inlined library code by file and opcode (SHFL.UP = prefix sum, SHFL.BFLY = top-k)
nsight_compute.kernel_metrics: duration share (base clocks), achieved/theoretical occupancy, threads per warp instruction, branch uniformity, SM/memory throughput, warp stall reasons incl. barrier, waves per SM
nsight_compute.limits: clocks locked to base and caches flushed per replay; use shares, not absolute times

analytic: decode_utilization.py computes from the index the useful-lane fraction of decode tiles and tiles per range (Nsight counts idle lanes executing zero-work tiles as active)
correctness: every saved top-10 of every profiled process compared with the CPU oracle (results/2026-11-11-cuda-bound-precision/inputs/cpu-top10-500.tsv, first 25 queries); monolithic post-timing validation must succeed
gpu_check: idle check before each profiled process (poll 30 s, abort after 30 min); 2-second GPU process sampler for the whole run, other users' home paths redacted as written
